text:
maria: Heads-up — onboarding run for quant4-miso on dedicated showed a tiny but reproducible token drift after long anchored prefill. Repro attached below, consistent across 3 runs but only when shard-swap coincides with warmup.

aj: can you paste the minimal repro command and a diff?

maria: sure — local runner command:
```
python tools/run_inference.py \
  --model miso-q4 --prefill-file tests/long_anchored_prompt.txt \
  --max-tokens 1024 --seed 42 --kv-mode prefill
```
outputs: two files: out_baseline.json out_quant4.json
small divergence at token index ~180 (prob mass shift ~1e-6) — looks like rounding w/ RoPE scale

ci-bot: CI failure on canary/quant4-miso #6789: long-anchored-regression detected. logs: https://ci.redwood/6789

kevin: interesting — shard swap during prefill could reorder KV writes. also quant rounding on rotary exponent could amplify in long-context.

diane: steps to triage: 1) reproduce with single-shard pinned, 2) reproduce with full-fp32 weights, 3) run with forced 32-bit accum for RoPE math. @ben can you queue an overnight bisect comparing quant variants and rotary clamp changes?

ben: queued. I'll run: quant4 vs quant8 vs fp32, with/without shard-swap, and with rotary-scale +/-1e-6 tweak. putting on canary tomorrow AM.

ops-bot: alert — node gpu-rtx-5 experienced OOM and triggered shard-rebalance at 1761112205; might coincide with the window maria hit.

sam: I reproduced locally on a smaller scale. seed 42 -> stable small divergence that grows if you extend warmup past 800 tokens. diff attached (delta in logit space). can share script.

maria: attached diffs and minimal repro script. hypothesis: RoPE scaling clamp or exponent accumulation under quantized kernel is not numerically stable for very long prefill + shard rebalancing. also saw slightly different KV indices after rebalance in debug dump.

aj: filing ticket LINK-4921 and adding the reproducer + CI job details. assigning to eng-ml.

diane: quick experiment: forcing 32-bit accum for the rotary exponent removed the stochastic drift but produced a deterministic mismatch (i.e., outputs changed but became stable). implies rounding at accumulation stage.

ben: plan: 1) add regression test to long-anchored suite that runs quant4+shard-swap path, 2) bisect kernel changes, 3) try 32-bit accum patch in kernel and measure perf impact.

maria: perf tradeoff note — 32-bit accum increases kernel time ~6% on our perf runs. still might be OK for Dedicated SLO on critical customers.

kevin: also check KV index packing logic — if rebalance reassigns shards mid-prefill we may be writing to different offsets; small rounding pushes token selection across boundary.

sam: will run the packed-index fuzz harness against quant kernels overnight.

maria: thanks all. I added reproduction artifacts to LINK-4921 and pinned the CI job. Next updates tomorrow after bisect.

aj: ack. :thumbsup:
